edits.old: Management, in one line Management is not the fork this question tests, so in one sentence: replace what is missing and cover what the defect exposes — immunoglobulin replacement for any low-IgG defect plus antibiotic prophylaxis (in-context; TMP-SMX as the agent is memory-sourced ⚠︎), no live vaccines ⚠︎, washed/IgA-depleted products instead of IVIG in selective IgA deficiency ⚠︎, and allogeneic HSCT as the only cure for CD40L deficiency ⚠︎.
edits.new: Long-term treatment, matched to the defect CVID and XLA — lifelong immunoglobulin replacement (IVIG); it replaces antibody but does not remove the autoimmune and malignancy risk of CVID · CD40 ligand deficiency — immunoglobulin replacement plus antibiotic prophylaxis (TMP-SMX ⚠︎); allogeneic HSCT is the only cure ⚠︎ · SCID — hematopoietic stem cell transplant as early as possible, with antiviral and antifungal prophylaxis until then · Complete DiGeorge (athymic) — cultured thymus tissue transplant: the marrow precursors are normal but have no thymus to mature in, so the graft is thymus, not marrow · Chronic granulomatous disease — interferon gamma with antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis · Selective IgA deficiency — no IVIG; washed or IgA-depleted blood products ⚠︎ · Any of these defects — no live vaccines ⚠︎
edits.why: Q6 tests long-term management, so the one-line management note becomes a masked defect-to-treatment grid: IVIG for CVID, HSCT for SCID, thymus transplant for DiGeorge, interferon gamma for CGD (all in the Q6 explanation); keeps the existing flags.

edits.old: atopic and autoimmune associations, granulomas, and lymphoma risk ⚠︎
edits.new: chronic diarrhea or an IBD-like enteropathy; asthma and later lung fibrosis; autoimmune disease (rheumatoid arthritis, thyroiditis); poor growth; granulomas ⚠︎; autoimmune disease and lymphoma risk persist on IVIG
